details: CONFIRMED by reproduction: a replica e-abc (chmod 500, sealed/ chmod 000) in the scratchpad survived
shutil.rmtree(p, ignore_errors=True) with all of sealed/, out/, config/ still listed. Before this change the tool
itself removed these folders (0 of the 174 trace folders of the two latest records exist), so the change turns a
clean /tmp into a leak of one folder per run on every paid run, and breaks the queue item's own pass case "a green
run leaves none" and the function's docstring "Either way the tool's temp folders are removed afterwards". The
new test passes only because its fixture folders are writable, so it passes with the removal effectively disabled
on real data. PLAUSIBLE extra: sealed/ is sealed by the tool on purpose (its content is unreadable to us); keeping it
indefinitely in /tmp is more exposure than the tool intended. Size: 15 minutes.
evidence: $ (replica) chmod 000 e-abc/sealed; chmod 500 e-abc; python3 -c "shutil.rmtree(p, ignore_errors=True)"
$ live records: 2026-10-26T01-47-23Z-master.json 81 runs, 0 folders exist; 2026-10-27T11-37-58Z-master.json 93 runs, 0 exist
failing_case: A paid batch of 93 runs, green. The eval tool, now called with --keep-temp, leaves /private/tmp/e-XXXX for each run with
mode dr-x------ on e-XXXX and d--------- on e-XXXX/sealed (as every one of the 178 existing /private/tmp/e-* folders
has). keep_traces calls shutil.rmtree(e-XXXX, ignore_errors=True): it cannot unlink entries of a read-only folder, the
error is swallowed, and all 93 folders stay (0.35-3 MB each, holding the run's config and the sealed/ part). Expected:
no e-XXXX folder of the batch is left; a red batch keeps only the copies under $RELAY_HOME/eval-traces.
fix_hint: Remove with an error handler that makes the failing entry's parent (and the entry, when a folder) owner-writable and
retries (os.chmod(..., 0o700); shutil.rmtree(..., onexc=...) on 3.12+, onerror before), or chmod -R u+rwx the e-*
folder with os.walk first; only after temp_folder() has matched. Make the test fixture mirror the real modes.
pass_cases: 1. Fixture run folder built like the real one (e-x/out/trace.jsonl, e-x/config/, e-x/sealed/ chmod 000, then e-x chmod
500), green batch: after bin/eval-record exits 0, e-x does not exist and $RELAY_HOME/eval-traces does not exist.
2. Same layout, red batch where run 2 fails a meaning grader: run 2's out/ is copied, keptTracePath names the copy,
its content equals the original trace; all three e-* folders are gone.
3. A folder that is not the tool's layout (tmp/mine/out/trace.jsonl) is never touched, chmod included.
4. The existing writable-folder tests keep passing.
reason: tests/test_eval_record.py fixtures now mirror real modes (sealed 000, top 500); green and red batch tests pass at head and fail at e742718.
findings.summary: the tool's real run folders are read-only (top r-x, sealed/ 000), so rmtree(ignore_errors=True) removes nothing: with --keep-temp every paid run now leaves all its ~90 folders in /tmp, green runs included

details: PLAUSIBLE (depends on how the tool cleans per run without --keep-temp; not measured). Rare path, bounded by macOS's
/tmp cleanup. Size: 15 minutes, or accept and note it.
failing_case: The eval tool dies after 40 runs without writing .ci/evals.json: bin/eval-record prints "wrote no record" and returns
before keep_traces, so the 40 kept e-* folders stay in /tmp. Before --keep-temp the tool removed them as it went
(per run). Expected: either they are removed or the leak is bounded and stated.
fix_hint: Accept and say so in the docstring, or have bin/ci sweep e-* folders created after the eval step started that hold
pass_cases: 1. No evals.json: exit 2 with "plugin evals wrote no record", as today.
2. A normal batch: unchanged behaviour (see F1).
reason: Accepted and stated in the keep_traces docstring (bin/eval-record:185-187).

details: CONFIRMED by reading report(): the trace line is appended only in the llm-fail branch. The queue item's pass case
("a path the record names") is met by the JSON. Size: 5 minutes.
failing_case: A red batch where run 2 errored: keep_traces copies run 2's out/ and sets keptTracePath, but the printed note
"run 2: the run errored (...)" carries no "trace:" line, so a person reading the gate log does not learn the copy
exists (it is only in the record JSON). Same for "FAIL ... code grader failed".
fix_hint: Append the trace line once per run that has keptTracePath, wherever its first FAIL or errored note is printed.
pass_cases: 1. Errored run in a red batch: the output holds "trace: <keptTracePath>" after its note.
2. Failed meaning grader: the existing "trace:" line stays.
reason: tests/test_eval_record.py test_an_errored_run_and_a_failed_code_grader_print_their_kept_trace passes at head, fails at e742718.
findings.summary: the printed report names the kept trace only under a failed meaning grader; an errored run or a failed code grader gets a copy but no printed path
